title: The Fifth Report on auctions in Bengal, 1796-98
body: The Fifth Report (1813) recorded that in Bengal the revenue was not realised with punctuality and lands were periodically exposed to sale by auction. In the native year 1203 (1796-97), the land advertised for sale carried a jumma (assessment) of sicca rupees 28,70,061; the land actually sold bore a jumma of 14,18,756; and the purchase money came to sicca rupees 17,90,416. In 1204 (1797-98), the land advertised was for sicca rupees 26,66,191, the quantity sold was for sicca rupees 22,74,076, and the purchase money was sicca rupees 21,47,580. The report added that among the defaulters were some of the oldest families of the country, such as the rajas of Nuddea, Rajeshaye and Bishenpore, whose estates were dismembered at the end of each succeeding year.
